steps.say: Numbers below zero are negative. We write them with a minus sign, like -3.
On a thermometer, temperatures below 0 °C are negative.

figure.alt: A thermometer from -10 °C to 10 °C. The liquid stops at -4 °C.

steps.say: -4 °C is colder than -1 °C, because it is further below zero.
To count across zero, count to 0 first, then keep going.

check.prompt: The temperature is -2 °C. It rises by 6 degrees. What is the temperature now?
hints: Rising means the temperature goes up.
check.explanation: From -2 up to 0 is 2 degrees. 4 more degrees makes 4 °C.

options.why: 0 °C is warmer than any temperature below zero.
2 °C is above zero, so it is warmer.
-3 °C is closer to zero, so it is warmer than -7 °C.

hints: The further below zero, the colder it is.
Picture the temperatures on a number line.
check.explanation: -7 °C is the furthest below zero, so it is the coldest.
